# Context
Causal-TimeBank is an English news corpus (183 TimeBank documents) annotated for
event causality. Event mentions are marked inline as <ID text>
(e.g. <ei3 acquired>, <ei7 said>). Use the eiid from each tag as the identifier.
Annotation is intra-sentence only: all pairs to classify are within the same sentence.

## Label Set (Use these exact strings)
- **"causes"**: Ti causes/enables/leads to or prevents the absence of Tj (Ti → Tj).
- **"causedby"**: Tj causes/enables/leads to or prevents the absence of Ti (Tj → Ti).
- **"norel"**: No causal link.

## What is annotated
A causal link requires a lexical anchor in the text; it is never inferred from world knowledge
or plausibility. The anchor is either a causal connective joining the two events (because,
because of, due to, as a result of, in the wake of, in response to, so, thus, since,
in exchange for, and causal by / from: "killed by the blast", "the loss stems from the
write-downs"), or a causative predicate taking one event as cause and the other as effect
(cause, lead to, result in, stem from, trigger, force, make, send, keep, allow, enable, help,
prevent, ensure, guarantee, bolster, reflect, follow). That bridging predicate is usually NOT
one of the two events you label: label the endpoints filling its cause and effect slots, which
often sit two or three mentions apart with other mentions in between — not the adjacent steps.
Everything else is norel, however sensible the causal story: purpose or intention (in talks to
settle the dispute, an attempt to get out), enablement chains you reconstruct yourself
(continuing → launching → programs), an event and its own sub-part or nominalisation
(suspending / trading, bought / purchase), a speaker's motives, mere temporal succession, and
transitive closure — given A → B and B → C, do not add A → C unless the text separately
expresses it. Most sentences contain no anchor and therefore no causal links.

# Output Format
- Use the eiid from each <ID text> tag as the identifier.
- Follow the provided JSON structure exactly.
- Use only the approved label strings: "causes", "causedby", "norel".
- Every listed pair must appear exactly once in the JSON.
- Every "causes" entry must be accompanied by its symmetric "causedby" entry.

If there are no pairs to classify, return an empty array [].

IMPORTANT:
No matter what reason step by step, then output the final JSON.
